Hi Lisa — great to hear you're ready. Quick answers and a proposed plan below; I've attached a short onboarding checklist and the ops runbook draft.

Summary answers:
- Backfill approach: we typically avoid a full stop-the-world migration. Our preferred pattern is a streamed bulk export -> staged ingest into a new vector index with incremental sync (dual reads during canary), followed by cutover. For 4.2M docs we recommend chunking into batches and running parallel workers.
- Index choice: FAISS HNSW (CPU) or GPU IVF+PQ depending on latency budgets. If you need sub-50ms tail latency for 100+ QPS, plan for GPU-based serving and sharded indexes.
- Rerank evals: we run NDCG@10, MRR, and precision@k on a labeled 1–5k query set; 2k is a good starting point. We'll also run blind A/B with interleaved traffic for a short canary.

What we need from you to scope accurately:
- S3 read-only export link for the corpus (or access to Pinecone export).
- A representative queries file + labeled relevance judgments (even partial).
- Target latency and expected peak QPS.

Proposed near-term timeline:
- Week 1 (Feb 22): Technical kickoff + access handoff (1h) — I've tentatively scheduled 2026-02-22 15:00 PT.
- Week 2: Backfill run + QA in staging (run duration depends on ingest parallelism).
- Week 3: Rerank evals and canary (A/B) to measure NDCG/MRR.

Owners (initial):

Marissa / team — adding some technical constraints and recommendations so we can scope hours: 

Backfill patterns (options):
1) Bulk -> build offline index (preferred if you can tolerate a short lag): export -> shard -> parallel ingest -> validate checksums -> swap. Advantage: consistent global index and simpler validation.
2) Dual-write + incremental catch-up (minimal downtime): start streaming new writes to both systems while bulk-building the new index; once parity is validated, route reads to new index. Extra complexity in sync but lower customer-visible impact.

Performance notes:
- For 4.2M docs, CPU HNSW can handle near-real-time queries at modest QPS (10–50) but tail latency will be higher at scale. For 100+ QPS with <80ms P95 consider GPU IVF+PQ + batched retrieval.
- Disk/RAM: expect ~0.6–1.2x raw corpus size in memory for HNSW; IVF+PQ trades memory for IVF centroids + quantized vectors.
- Vector quantization: we will evaluate 8-bit vs 4-bit quantization in staging, run small AB tests to measure downstream rerank quality. Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization profiles per workload.

Operational hooks we need to provide:
- Checkpointing for idempotent ingest workers
- Per-batch validation metrics (ingest rate, failed docs, vector norm distributions)
- A canary traffic slice (1% -> 10%) with automated rollback if NDCG drops > 2 points versus baseline

I will prepare:
- backfill-run-scripts (bash + k8s job manifests)
- quick capacity worksheet (GPU / mem / node counts)
- short checklist for data hygiene (duplicate IDs, text length buckets)

Estimated effort: 4–6 engineer-days for runbook + 2–3 engineer-days to run the first staged backfill (depending on access + export speed).

—Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
